assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstration that TNF is the dominant driver of synovial inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis and that blocking it produces clinical benefit. This changed a disabling disease and opened cytokine-targeted therapy across rheumatology, gastroenterology and dermatology. Concept is clear, original and clinically transformative.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini are the two credited names and the intellectual and clinical partnership is well documented, so a two-person prize is clean. Other contributors (antibody engineering, industrial development) are not on the supplied credit list.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of real-world and trial evidence, with multiple independent agents and indications. Recognition is fully mature and, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether credit for antibody engineering and drug development outside the supplied names would be seen as necessary.
I am recalling details from memory and have not independently verified the history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Elucidation of GLP-1 as an incretin hormone and its translation into long-acting agonists that treat type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit. The physiological discovery and the therapeutic impact are both of exceptional scale and current relevance.
assessment.attribution: Credit is distributed among basic physiology (Holst, Drucker, Mojsov on the active peptide form) and drug development (Knudsen). A three-person prize drawn from the physiologists is plausible, but the peptide-identification contribution and the allocation between academic and industrial work are contested.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy is established by large independent trials and wide use; long-term outcome data are still accumulating. Timing is highly favorable.
uncertainties: Contested priority regarding the active GLP-1 fragment.
Handling of industrial development credit (Knudsen), which I leave outside the three names.
Habener and others not on this list may also be relevant.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies; a new therapeutic modality with growing application including early autoimmune disease trials.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain made the decisive CAR design and clinical translation contributions; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T cells. Other early CAR originators (Eshhar, others) are not on the list, so the configuration is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and independent long-term remissions; toxicity, access and solid tumor limits remain, but the core achievement is solid.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric receptor concept is not represented in the supplied names.
Choice between Rosenberg and other credited persons is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishment of long-term self-organizing organoid cultures from single Lgr5 adult stem cells, a platform now used throughout disease modeling, host-pathogen work, cancer and regenerative research.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the conceptual and stem-cell work and Sato performed the key culture advance; two-person configuration is clear. Other organoid traditions (pluripotent-derived) are outside this candidate.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted and reproduced worldwide; clinical translation still emerging, but the tool's impact is already established.
uncertainties: Whether Sato's role would be viewed as sufficiently separate from the Clevers laboratory discovery.
Translational medical impact is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the unfolded protein response, a signaling pathway from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, of broad importance for proteostasis, secretory cell physiology, and disease including diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori made the decisive mechanistic discoveries (Ire1/Hac1 splicing and signaling); other contributors such as Kohno or Ron could be argued. A two-person prize seems fair.
assessment.maturity: Foundational and extensively confirmed over three decades; therapeutic application via UPR modulators is still early, but the biology is stable.
uncertainties: Competing credit claims within the UPR field.
Direct clinical consequence is less developed than for other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational targeting of BCR-ABL with imatinib turned CML from a fatal disease into a chronic one, and established the paradigm of kinase-directed cancer therapy, with resistance mechanisms informing next-generation agents.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical translation), Lydon (compound and program) and Sawyers (resistance biology and second-generation agents) form a plausible trio. Industrial chemistry contributions (e.g., Zimmermann) and Rowley/others on the Philadelphia chromosome are outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: more than two decades of survival data and many successors.
uncertainties: Whether Sawyers or another credited name is better placed than the three chosen.
Prior recognition of related work elsewhere may complicate the case.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of cGAS and STING as the pathway sensing cytosolic DNA and driving type I interferon responses, central to antiviral defense, autoimmunity (interferonopathies, lupus), and cancer immunity. This resonates with interferon-mediated autoimmune disease mechanisms.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP, Barber discovered STING; other credited names (Ishikawa, Sun, Wu) are contributors but less likely central. Allocation is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism strongly confirmed; therapeutic agents (STING agonists and inhibitors) have so far had limited clinical success, so impact on medicine is still partly prospective.
uncertainties: Clinical translation is not yet demonstrated.
Priority between groups on STING (Barber, Ishikawa, others) may be argued.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR as a central regulator of growth and metabolism, with consequences for cancer, immunosuppression, diabetes and ageing. The molecular pathway is of broad importance across biology.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR; Sabatini identified mammalian mTOR components and nutrient sensing. Schreiber's contribution on rapamycin targets is related but I leave it out. Prior honors for Hall exist, and Sabatini's reputation has been affected by non-scientific controversies, which could matter.
assessment.maturity: Core biology firmly established; clinical use (rapalogs) is real though more modest than the biology suggests.
uncertainties: Potential non-scientific considerations around one proposed laureate.
Whether clinical impact is sufficient relative to other candidates.
